question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{55}$ be a random sample of size $n=55$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3}, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.11,$ calculate $P(1.6<\overset{―}{X}<1.7).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ | $\,0.9788\,$ | $\,0.9793\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ | $\,0.9834\,$ | $\,0.9838\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9868\,$ | $\,0.9871\,$ | $\,0.9875\,$ |

Given that the population variance $\sigma^2 = 0.5,$ calculate $P( \overline{X}>1.9 ).$

*Hint: A table of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\, -1.5 \,$ | $\, 0.0655 \,$ | $\, 0.0643 \,$ | $\, 0.0630 \,$ |

current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose that $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu$ and population standard deviation $\sigma.$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overline{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overline{X}\sim N\!\left(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =100,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}x\cdot \frac{2}{9}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{2}{9}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{2{x}^{3}}{27}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is $\sigma^2 = 0.5.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(2,\frac{0.5}{100}) \\  & ∼N(2,0.005).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P( \overline{X}>1.9 ).$ So, we convert $\overline{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>1.9) & =P(Z>\frac{1.9-2}{\sqrt{0.005}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-1.41).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>-1.41) & =1-P(Z\le -1.41) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.41).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have that

$$
\Phi(-1.41) = 0.0793.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>1.9) & =1-Φ(-1.41) \\  & =1-0.0793 \\  & =0.9207.\end{aligned}
$$
